beats.subline: Monday, November 2, 2026 close — a tech-led pullback as AI-spending worries persisted, while oil prices plunged on hopes for an Iran diplomatic breakthrough.
beats.body: Tech shares extended October's AI-spending selloff, dragging the S&P 500 and Nasdaq lower even as the Dow gained on rotation into non-tech sectors; crude oil tumbled roughly 7-8% on reports the US and Iran are pursuing a diplomatic resolution, and investors looked ahead to Tuesday's midterm elections.

beats.body: No qualifying international story distinct from the Iran/Hormuz and Taiwan items elsewhere in this brief could be confirmed within the 72-hour window; checks on Israel's coalition crisis, Venezuela's transition talks, and US-China trade all traced back to mid-October or earlier.

beats.headline: Taiwan accuses China of 'cognitive warfare' after a surge in incursions
beats.body: Taiwan's Defense Ministry logged 32 Chinese aircraft sorties and seven naval vessels in the 24 hours through November 1, with 26 aircraft crossing the Strait's median line, while its coast guard accused Beijing of using staged law-enforcement patrols near the Pratas and Kinmen islands to manufacture a false claim of authority over Taiwan's waters.

beats.headline: US carries out limited strikes in Strait of Hormuz as Netanyahu pushes for a broader campaign
beats.body: A US official said American forces struck Iranian targets, including on Qeshm Island, after Iranian forces used surface-to-air missiles against US assets near the Strait of Hormuz; Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is separately lobbying Trump for a renewed air campaign after the midterms, though Trump has made no decision and had said no new strikes would come before Tuesday's election.

beats.headline: Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows revenue tripling but losses mounting
beats.body: Anthropic's updated S-1 reported $33.2 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026 against a $104 billion net loss, driven mainly by swings in the value of convertible notes, and disclosed about $895.4 billion in aggregate compute and infrastructure purchase commitments as the company heads toward an IPO roadshow.

beats.headline: byFaith publishes its quarterly roundup of PCA pastoral transitions
beats.body: The magazine's July-September 2026 ministry transitions list reports 37 pastoral moves across the denomination, including Fred Greco's move from senior pastor at Christ Church in Katy, Texas to PCA Stated Clerk, along with 11 deaths of PCA ministers during the quarter.
